Finding 01 / coordination

One strong worker is the default

Inside one tightly coupled outcome, coordination has to earn its cost.

Research noteEvidence pack / current programmeQualification preserved

More autonomous minds look like more capacity. Inside one tightly coupled outcome, they can instead create more surfaces to brief, synchronise, integrate and review.

What we observed

Several controlled arrangements compared a strong end-to-end worker with specialist chains or multi-worker assemblies. On complete-outcome economics, the one-worker shape often won. Decomposability was necessary but not sufficient. A seam also had to produce independently valuable evidence or expertise.

The exception matters.

One sequential two-specialist marketing chain won blind quality. Two-operator-plus-assembler sales and three-worker research arrangements lost.

What changed

The organisation now starts wide and shallow: one accountable lead with one Staff producer. Another worker is added only when a stable specialism, independent evidence, local closure or context limit can repay the coordination cost.

What this does not prove

It is not a universal solo-agent rule. It does not show that one worker wins every domain, scale or model mix. It establishes a default that must be displaced by evidence, not headcount optimism.
